headline: The FedRAMP caveat on AWS CloudTrail ingestion is dropped; SaaS AI agent onboarding links resolve
summary_md:
- **AWS CloudTrail** loses the paragraph advising against ingesting data from an AWS commercial environment into a FedRAMP-certified Cortex XSIAM tenant.
- **SaaS AI Agent Security** replaces all eight `broken-reference` placeholders on the onboarding index with real per-platform paths.
- Nothing else moved: the only other change is a wording tweak to the Attack Surface Management overview's description.

highlights.title: The FedRAMP warning on ingesting AWS commercial data is gone
highlights.detail: The paragraph saying Palo Alto Networks does not recommend ingesting data from an AWS commercial environment into a FedRAMP-certified Cortex XSIAM tenant, and to contact Customer Support if you must, was deleted with nothing put in its place.

highlights.title: Eight SaaS AI agent onboarding links stop pointing at broken-reference
highlights.detail: Atlassian Rovo, Box AI Agents, ChatGPT Enterprise, Cursor Enterprise, Gemini Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio and ServiceNow AI Platform each now link to a page under onboard-saas-ai-agents/.

items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsia: Removes the recommendation against ingesting AWS commercial environment data into a FedRAMP-certified tenant, and the pointer to Customer Support with it.
items.xsiam/cloud-security/cortex-cloud-saas-s: All eight platform links on the onboarding index change from broken-reference placeholders to relative paths under onboard-saas-ai-agents/.
items.xsiam/detect-investigate-and-respond-to-: The page description now expands Attack Surface Management to "(ASM)" on first use; the body is untouched.
